note: Dark spy comedy set in Chile in 1973, just before the coup: CIA agents Chris (Malkovich) and Lee (Rockwell), dispatched by station chief MJ (Buscemi) from Santiago to Easter Island. McDonagh's first film since The Banshees of Inisherin (Searchlight). Premiered at Venice Sept 2026 to a ~14-minute ovation; Malkovich won the Volpi Cup for Best Actor. Not streaming yet — surfaces when it opens. Dave asked for it by name during the 49ers game, likely a trailer spot.

title: Wild Horse Nine

note: A24 documentary. Fielder embeds with Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes and her partner Billy Evans during the 34 days before Holmes reported to federal prison; what began as a month of filming became a three-year project. Secret-screening premiere at Telluride (Sep 6, 2026); Certified Fresh on Rotten Tomatoes; opened to ~$15.6M on 855 screens (biggest non-concert documentary opening since Fahrenheit 9/11), ~$45M domestic through Oct 25. THEATRICAL ONLY for now. Playing this week in Sacramento (Cinemark Century DOCO, Regal Delta Shores) and listed at El Dorado Hills, the closest screens to Fiddletown — checked Oct 26.
title: You Can See Everything

cast: Dennis Christopher, Dennis Quaid, Daniel Stern, Jackie Earle Haley
note: The cycling classic: in Bloomington, Indiana, 19-year-old Dave Stoller — obsessed with the Italian Cinzano racing team, Italian opera, Italian everything — and his three 'cutter' friends take on the Indiana University establishment in the Little 500 bike race. Steve Tesich's script won the Oscar for Best Original Screenplay. A natural for Dave: former competitive cyclist, and the hero's name is a bonus. Not on any subscription service right now — rent or buy only (checked Oct 29).
status: Rent/buy only — Apple TV, Amazon, Fandango At Home ($3.99 rent)

title: Midnight Mass

cast: Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Val Kilmer, Natalie Portman, Ashley Judd
note: Mann's cat-and-mouse epic: Neil McCauley's disciplined L.A. robbery crew against Vincent Hanna, the detective hunting them — De Niro and Pacino's first film truly opposite each other, with the downtown bank-shootout set piece everything since gets measured against. A big-commitment classic at just under three hours. It arrived on Netflix US on Oct 16, 2026, with Mann's Heat 2 on the way.
status: Streaming on Netflix and Prime Video; free with ads on Plex
title: Heat

cast: Michael Keaton, Nick Offerman, John Carroll Lynch, Laura Dern
note: Keaton as Ray Kroc, the Illinois milkshake-mixer salesman who talked his way into the McDonald brothers' revolutionary San Bernardino burger stand in 1954 — then franchised it into an empire and took the name, the system, and eventually the real estate out from under them. A business story with a sting: persistence, vision, and exactly where ambition crosses into ruthlessness. Dave asked for it by name.
status: Streaming on Netflix; rent/buy on Amazon, Apple TV, Fandango
title: The Founder

creator: Shuichi Shigeno (manga)
note: The street-racing legend: Takumi Fujiwara, a tofu-delivery kid in his dad's humble Toyota AE86 Sprinter Trueno, turns out to be the fastest downhill racer on Mt. Akina — beating RX-7s and GT-Rs on pure feel while barely caring about cars. Eurobeat soundtrack, gutter runs, and a slow-burn coming-of-age story across six stages. Foundational car-culture anime — for a lifelong car guy, this is homework of the best kind. Also the likely answer to Dave's hanging 'this is it' from Nov 3.
source: Dave — asked Nov 6 (possibly the title left hanging Nov 3)
